explanation: Mathlib's `Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup` (Mathlib/GroupTheory/MonoidLocalization/GrothendieckGroup.lean) only provides the localization-based construction (`GrothendieckGroup`/`GrothendieckAddGroup`, `of`, `instCommGroup`, `inv_mk`, `mk_div_mk`, `lift`, `lift_apply`). It has no multiplication, no `mulAddHom`, and no ring instances on the Grothendieck completion, so there is no statement about `mulAddHom (of 1) x = x` to duplicate. Searches for `mulAddHom`, `lift₂`, `NonAssocSemiring`/`Semiring` together with `Grothendieck`, and for `addMonoidOf` in Mathlib turned up only the affine-monoid usage `GrothendieckAddGroup M` for `Module.finrank`, i.e. nothing ring-theoretic. The result depends on the library's own definition `Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup.mulAddHom` and is not present in Mathlib, Batteries or Lean core.
